title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East (show b- Late?) on 1970-01-02
source: Soundboard > 7 1/2' Reel Master @ 7.5 ips (Recorded By Bear on a Sony 770 Reel Deck) > 1st gen (TDK SAX-100 cassette) from Dick Latvala (Master Reel Playback on a Technics 1506 Reel to Reel > Tascam 122 MK111 Cassette Deck No dolby) > Analog to Digital (Cassettes played back on Nakamichi Dragon > Sony PCM-R700 DAT @ 44.1 by Jim Wise 1998); Edited and mastered SIRMIck

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture with TC front‑and‑center, featuring a fiery Dark Star and Tighten Up jam that make this early‑1970 show a fan favorite.
ai_review.review: The recording is a very good‑quality soundboard mix that highlights Tom Constanten’s keyboards (TC) while the bass can be a bit recessed. Musically the performance shines on Dark Star, Feelin’ Groovy and an incendiary Tighten Up sequence with a standout Bob Weir solo, though some listeners felt the first set never fully “takes off.”

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars and praise both the performance (especially Dark Star and Tighten Up) and the soundboard quality; a few minor criticisms (mix balance, minimalistic Dark Star) keep the rating just below “exceptional.”

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp overall mix with Tom Constanten prominently up in the mix; some listeners note Phil’s bass is recessed, but no major drop‑outs or distortion reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The show opens strong with tight harmonies but some feel it never reaches the instrumental heights of late‑‘69; the second half builds momentum with extended jams that peak on Dark Star and Tighten Up.

band_member_comments.Phil: Mix makes Phil's bass hard to hear, affecting his presence in the recording.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir delivers a notable solo during the Tighten Up jam and is praised for his guitar work throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s keyboards are unusually forward in the mix, giving the performance a kaleidoscopic vibe.
